ClientAgentLlm.description:
The typed `llm:` policy block of an agent's config document (lane agent-llm-policy): the
provider the agent is pinned to, its default model hint, and a hard placement constraint.
Every field is optional. On create/update the block is replaced as a whole; `{}` clears it.

makes the agent's LLM calls fail closed (never a silent fallback).

ClientAspectField.description:
A field of the aspect: its type (`string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `datetime`, `duration`,
`enum`, `list<string>`, `list<datetime>`), enum values, default, declared transitions
(`from → [to…]`), whether inline items inherit it from their file, whether the host derives
it (a derived field is never written by a client), and how clients present it.

Besides its declared fields, an aspect lists each promoted column it presents: `title` and
`type` (strings) and `updated_at` (a datetime the host maintains, so `derived`). Views and
queries may name these three columns whether the aspect presents them or not. A promoted
column's value is the row's own `title`, `type` or `updated_at`, not an entry of the row's
`fields`.

display.description: How clients present the field; absent when the aspect declares nothing for it.

ClientAspectFieldDisplay.description: How clients present a field. Every key is optional.

format.description:
One of `text`, `number`, `priority` (a higher value is more urgent), `checkbox`, `badge`
(an enum value takes its tone), `tags`, `person`, `date`, `datetime`, `relative` (a
moment relative to now), `duration`, `recurrence` (an RFC 5545 rule) and `timezone` (an
IANA zone name). An unknown value renders as `text`. When absent, infer the format from
the type: string → `text`, integer → `number`, boolean → `checkbox`, datetime and
list<datetime> → `datetime`, duration → `duration`, enum → `badge`, list<string> →
`tags`. Under `date` and `datetime`, a value written without a time of day is that
calendar day, shown as written; an instant renders in the zone named by the record's
field formatted `timezone`, if it has one, else in the viewer's zone.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description:
The field's name for people (a column header, a form label), as plain text (render it
as text, never as markup).

values.description:
Enum fields: the presentation of each value the aspect presents, in the enum's declared
order.

ClientAspectOperation.description:
A declared logic operation bound to a pack skill tool; `available` says whether the tool
is installed right now (`:apply` answers `module_unavailable` otherwise).

ClientAspectOrderKey.description:
One ordering key of a declared query or view: an aspect field or a promoted column, and
its direction.

ClientAspectQuery.description: A named query, the argument names / types it takes, and the order its rows come in.

order.description:
The order the host returns the rows in. The host puts missing values last in both
directions and compares text by code point (so an enum orders by its text, not by its
declared order), integers numerically and datetimes chronologically. Empty = newest
first (`updated_at` descending).

ClientAspectValueDisplay.description: How clients present one enum value.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description:
The value's name for people (a badge, a board lane title), as plain text (render it as
text, never as markup).

tone.description:
One of `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error` and `muted`: a semantic name a
client maps onto its own palette, never a color. An unknown value renders as `neutral`.

ClientAspectView.description:
A declared view: `kind` ∈ `list | table | board | calendar | form` (the GenUI catalog maps
each kind to one component) and the query whose rows it renders (every kind but a form has
one).

columns.description:
The fields the view shows, in order: a list or table row's cells (the first is the
primary line), a board card's fields (the first is the card title), a calendar event's
details, a form's inputs (a `derived` field renders read-only). Each is an aspect field
or a promoted column (`title`, `type`, `updated_at`); a form shows neither `type` nor
`updated_at`. Empty = the client chooses.

group_by.description:
A board's lanes (GenUI `Board.columns`): the values of this enum field in declared
order, each with the label and tone the field's `display` gives it. On a list or table
it makes sections. A calendar or form has none.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description:
The view's name for people (a tab title, say), as plain text (render it as text, never
as markup).

order.description:
The order a client presents the rows in, within each lane or section when grouped.
Empty = the query's own `order`. It reorders only the rows the query returned and never
changes which rows come back, so a page cut at the query's limit is not the top rows by
this order. Every client compares the same way: missing values last in both directions;
an enum by its declared position; datetimes chronologically, a date without a time of
day counting as 00:00 UTC; integers numerically; `false` before `true`; text by Unicode
code point; rows that compare equal keep the order the query returned them in.

ClientAspect.description:
One aspect: a named bundle of fields, queries, views and operations a record gains when
any of its `key` fields is present, and how clients present it. Every presentation key
(labels, icons, formats, tones, the default view, the view order, a view's order) is
optional, and a client renders without it.

default_view.description: The view a client opens first, never a `form`. Absent = the client chooses.

fields.description: The declared fields, plus each promoted column the aspect presents; sorted by name.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description: The aspect's name for people, as plain text (render it as text, never as markup).

view_order.description:
The views a client lists (as tabs, say), in this order. A view left out is still
declared and reachable by name, typically a form that opens on a record. Empty = the
client chooses.

ClientAspect.title: ClientAspect

body means all retained history. Bounds are honoured at second granularity (floored /
ceiled), so a window can only include MORE rows than requested, never fewer.

model.description: Default model hint (an alias key or a literal model id); an explicit per-call model wins.

provider.description:

ClientCreateAgentRequest.description: The body of `POST /client/agents`. The idempotency key is envelope-level.

agent_id.description:
The handle (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`). Optional: when absent it is derived from
`display_name` (lower-cased, spaces → `-`, other characters dropped; `-2`, `-3`… on a
collision; `agent-<n>` when nothing survives). The immutable id is minted server-side.

capabilities.description: Capability ids requested for the child (must be a subset of the parent's).

config_yaml.description: Optional initial config document written after materialization.

llm.description:
Optional `llm:` policy block written into the new agent's config document (after
`config_yaml`, so it wins over a block the document may carry). `{}` writes nothing.

parent.description: Parent handle; defaults to the root agent.

template_ref.description:
The template the child is materialized from (also recorded in the parent's declared
hierarchy so the child is re-materialized at the next daemon start).

workspace_path.description: Directory RELATIVE TO THE PARENT's workspace; defaults to `agent_id`.

ClientCreateAgentRequest.title: ClientCreateAgentRequest

ClientProviderAgentCli.description:
An `agent-cli` entry's vendor CLI (ADR 2026-09-28): which vendor, the absolute path of the
user's own unmodified binary, and extra args appended after the fixed no-tools recipe.
Echoed in summaries (a client renders the vendor and offers the vendor's own sign-in
command); it carries no credential.

ClientProviderCost.description: Per-million-token prices (USD) of one provider entry.

ClientProviderRateLimit.description: The provider's rate limit (required by the runtime for every entry).

ClientProviderSidecar.description:
A local-class provider's sidecar launch spec. Request-only: an absolute host command path is
never echoed back (summaries report `sidecar_present`).

ClientCreateProviderRequest.description: The body of `POST /client/providers`. Carries NO key material — keys go through `:set-key`.

agent_cli.description: Required for (and only valid on) `backend_class: agent-cli`.

api_key_secret.description:
Secret reference name; defaults to `<provider_id>-api-key`, or for a `chatgpt-oauth`
entry to `<provider_id>-chatgpt-<first 8 hex digits of the daemon's host id>`. A
`chatgpt-oauth` entry that names a secret already holding a value (or already holding a
sign-in record) is refused with `already_exists`: the sign-in writes its access token
under that name.

auth_source.description:
`api-key` (default) | `chatgpt-oauth`. Fixed at creation. `chatgpt-oauth` is only valid
on `cloud-http` with `backend` absent or `openai-responses` and `auth_scheme` absent or
`bearer`; such an entry takes no key (`:set-key` is refused) and signs in instead.

rate_limit.description: Required (the runtime refuses an entry without a rate limit).

ClientCreateProviderRequest.title: ClientCreateProviderRequest

ClientDeleteAgentRequest.description: The body of `POST /client/agents/{agent_id}:delete` (a `null` body means the defaults).

remove_workspace.description:
`false` (default): terminate the agent and remove only its `.agent/` marker directory, so
the directory stops being agent-managed but its content survives. `true`: also remove the
whole workspace directory (containment-guarded; never the root workspace).

ClientDeleteAgentRequest.title: ClientDeleteAgentRequest

ClientEntityApplyRequest.description:
`POST /client/entities/{entity_id}:apply` body: a schema-declared operation and its
arguments (validated against the declaration by the host).
ClientEntityApplyRequest.title: ClientEntityApplyRequest

ClientEntityCreateRequest.description:
`POST /client/entities:create` body: a new inline item under the file at `parent`
(workspace-relative path); `record` is the item's fields (`id` is assigned by the host).
ClientEntityCreateRequest.title: ClientEntityCreateRequest

ClientOrderKey.description: One ordering key of an ad-hoc filter.

ClientEntityFilter.description: An ad-hoc filter (the projection's query surface): every clause is optional and ANDed.

parent.description: Restrict to the inline items of this file entity.

ClientEntityFilter.title: ClientEntityFilter

ClientEntityRow.description: One entity row (a file record, an inline item, or a directory's `index.md`).

anchor.description: The inline item's id inside `path`'s `items[]`; absent for a file / directory record.

aspects.description: The aspects the record has, sorted.

fields.description: Every frontmatter field of the record (declared and free-form).

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the file holding the record (an item: its parent file).

ClientEnvelope.$comment: Envelope invariant: exactly one of `data`/`error` is non-null (data XOR error).

ClientError.description:
A projected, client-safe error. `code` is the stable compatibility surface; `message` is
human-facing; `details` carries structured hints (e.g. the supported version range).

ClientErrorCode.description:
The deterministic Client API error codes (MODULE-020 §2.8). Adding codes is
backward-compatible per §2.12 (no `api_version` bump). `Unknown` is a forward-compat
catch-all so a client built against an older schema tolerates a newer server code on the
wire instead of failing to deserialize; the server never *produces* `Unknown`.

oneOf.description: A create named an agent id / workspace territory that already exists.
The request failed validation (id charset, path containment, bounds, document schema).
Forward-compat catch-all (deserialization only; never emitted by this server).

ClientWarning.description: A non-fatal, client-safe advisory attached to any envelope (e.g. an idempotent-replay note).

ClientEnvelope.description:
The versioned response envelope. `data` XOR `error` is non-null; `warnings` may accompany
either. Matches MODULE-020 §2.3 / §2.4.

`Debug` is hand-written to redact the `data` payload: a response envelope's data may carry a
secret (e.g. the login response's bearer/CSRF tokens), so `{:?}` on an envelope must never
print it (§2.14 — "response body before projection" is a never-log field). `error` (a stable
code + message) is shown.

ClientProviderPreflightResult.description:
One preflight verdict (`:set-key` / `:preflight`). `reason` is a fixed vocabulary: the
`LlmError` variant name (`model-not-available`, `provider-error`, …), `timeout`, `cancelled`,
`missing-key`, `missing-provider`, or `unsupported-backend-class`. For an `agent-cli` entry
the check is the vendor CLI's own sign-in status: ok = signed in; else `not-signed-in`,
`cli-not-found`, `cli-failed`, `daemon-identity-unknown`, `timeout`, `cancelled`. For a
`chatgpt-oauth` entry the check renews the sign-in when needed and lists the account's models
with it: ok = usable; else `not-signed-in` (no sign-in of this daemon), `session-ended` (sign
in again), `plan-usage-not-granted` (the account did not grant use of its plan; sign in again
to consent), `refresh-unavailable` (the credential expired and could not be renewed right
now), `unavailable` (the sign-in or the model list could not be reached), `timeout`.

ClientProviderKeyResult.description:
The result of `:set-key`: whether the key was stored (only after a passing preflight for
`cloud-http`) and the preflight verdict (absent when preflight was skipped).
ClientProviderKeyResult.title: ClientProviderKeyResult

ClientProviderRateLimit.description: The provider's rate limit (required by the runtime for every entry).

ClientProviderSignIn.description:
The sign-in state of a `chatgpt-oauth` entry (`GET /client/providers/{id}/sign-in`, the
result of `:sign-in-cancel`, and `sign_in` on the entry's summary). Never a token.

account.description: The signed-in account's own label (an email) — shown back to the user.

expires_at_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds. `pending`: when the attempt is abandoned. `signed-in`: when the
current credential lapses (the daemon renews it before then).

models.description: The models the account may use, when the provider listed them.

plan_usage.description: Once signed in: whether the account granted use of its plan for model requests.

reason.description:
A fixed token saying why the state is what it is, when there is something to say:
`timeout`, `cancelled`, `access-denied`, `authorization-failed`, `state-mismatch`,
`registration-incomplete`, `client-mismatch`, `account-mismatch`, `exchange-failed`,
`id-token-invalid`, `plan-usage-not-granted`, `session-ended`, `refresh-unavailable`,
`store-failed`, `unavailable`, `not-signed-in`. `signed-out` with `unavailable` means
this daemon cannot sign the entry in, and `:sign-in` is refused (`module_unavailable`):
either the entry's secret holds another installation's sign-in (an entry created under
another secret name signs in here), or this installation's host id cannot be read (no
entry signs in until it is repaired).

state.description:
`signed-out` | `pending` (an attempt is waiting for the browser) | `signed-in` |
`failed` (the last attempt ended without a session; see `reason`).

ClientProviderSignInModel.description: One model the signed-in account may use, as the provider lists it.

ClientProviderSummary.description:
One provider entry (`GET /client/providers` rows, `GET /client/providers/{id}`, and the
response of every entry mutation).

agent_cli.description: `agent-cli` entries only: the vendor CLI this entry drives.

auth_scheme.description: `bearer | x-api-key | api-key`; absent = the backend's default.

auth_source.description:
Where the entry's credential comes from, when it is not an operator-entered key:
`chatgpt-oauth` (a Sign in with ChatGPT session the daemon keeps fresh). Absent = an
API key (`key` says whether one is stored).

endpoint.description: Connect URL for `cloud-http`; may be empty for other classes.

last_usage.description: `agent-cli` entries: the last allowance read this daemon made (in-memory).

sidecar_present.description: Whether the entry carries a sidecar launch spec (the spec itself is never echoed).

sign_in.description: `chatgpt-oauth` entries only: the sign-in state at the time of the read.

ClientProviderUsage.description:
The subscription allowance behind an `agent-cli` entry, read through the vendor CLI's own
account surface (ADR 2026-09-28 §usage): Claude Code's `/usage`, Codex's app-server
`account/rateLimits/read`, Grok Build's `x.ai/billing`. Never a model turn, never a token
read. `reason` (when not ok) is the sign-in probe's vocabulary plus `unparsed` (the CLI
answered something this version does not read) and `unsupported-backend-class`. A
`chatgpt-oauth` entry always answers `ok: false` with `not-provided`: its plan allowance has
no API (a client links to the vendor's own usage page instead).

account.description: The signed-in account's own label (an email) — shown back to the user, never persisted.

plan.description: The plan the vendor names (`max`, `plus`, `supergrok_heavy`, …), verbatim.

ClientProviderUsageWindow.description:
One allowance window an `agent-cli` vendor reported (`GET /client/providers/{id}/usage`).
`used_percent` is 0..=100 as the vendor states it.

kind.description:
`session` (Claude's 5-hour window) | `week` | `week-model` | `primary` | `secondary`
(Codex's rolling windows) | `period` (Grok's weekly or monthly pool) | `other`.

label.description: The vendor's own wording (`Current week (all models)`, `5-hour`, `Weekly limit`).

resets_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the window resets, when the vendor states an instant.

resets_label.description: The vendor's own reset wording when only text is known.

providers.description: YAML order; exactly the first entry (if any) is `selected`.

ClientAspect.description:
One aspect: a named bundle of fields, queries, views and operations a record gains when
any of its `key` fields is present, and how clients present it. Every presentation key
(labels, icons, formats, tones, the default view, the view order, a view's order) is
optional, and a client renders without it.

default_view.description: The view a client opens first, never a `form`. Absent = the client chooses.

fields.description: The declared fields, plus each promoted column the aspect presents; sorted by name.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description: The aspect's name for people, as plain text (render it as text, never as markup).

view_order.description:
The views a client lists (as tabs, say), in this order. A view left out is still
declared and reachable by name, typically a form that opens on a record. Empty = the
client chooses.

ClientAspectField.description:
A field of the aspect: its type (`string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `datetime`, `duration`,
`enum`, `list<string>`, `list<datetime>`), enum values, default, declared transitions
(`from → [to…]`), whether inline items inherit it from their file, whether the host derives
it (a derived field is never written by a client), and how clients present it.

Besides its declared fields, an aspect lists each promoted column it presents: `title` and
`type` (strings) and `updated_at` (a datetime the host maintains, so `derived`). Views and
queries may name these three columns whether the aspect presents them or not. A promoted
column's value is the row's own `title`, `type` or `updated_at`, not an entry of the row's
`fields`.

display.description: How clients present the field; absent when the aspect declares nothing for it.

ClientAspectFieldDisplay.description: How clients present a field. Every key is optional.

format.description:
One of `text`, `number`, `priority` (a higher value is more urgent), `checkbox`, `badge`
(an enum value takes its tone), `tags`, `person`, `date`, `datetime`, `relative` (a
moment relative to now), `duration`, `recurrence` (an RFC 5545 rule) and `timezone` (an
IANA zone name). An unknown value renders as `text`. When absent, infer the format from
the type: string → `text`, integer → `number`, boolean → `checkbox`, datetime and
list<datetime> → `datetime`, duration → `duration`, enum → `badge`, list<string> →
`tags`. Under `date` and `datetime`, a value written without a time of day is that
calendar day, shown as written; an instant renders in the zone named by the record's
field formatted `timezone`, if it has one, else in the viewer's zone.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description:
The field's name for people (a column header, a form label), as plain text (render it
as text, never as markup).

values.description:
Enum fields: the presentation of each value the aspect presents, in the enum's declared
order.

ClientAspectOperation.description:
A declared logic operation bound to a pack skill tool; `available` says whether the tool
is installed right now (`:apply` answers `module_unavailable` otherwise).

ClientAspectOrderKey.description:
One ordering key of a declared query or view: an aspect field or a promoted column, and
its direction.

ClientAspectQuery.description: A named query, the argument names / types it takes, and the order its rows come in.

order.description:
The order the host returns the rows in. The host puts missing values last in both
directions and compares text by code point (so an enum orders by its text, not by its
declared order), integers numerically and datetimes chronologically. Empty = newest
first (`updated_at` descending).

ClientAspectValueDisplay.description: How clients present one enum value.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description:
The value's name for people (a badge, a board lane title), as plain text (render it as
text, never as markup).

tone.description:
One of `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error` and `muted`: a semantic name a
client maps onto its own palette, never a color. An unknown value renders as `neutral`.

ClientAspectView.description:
A declared view: `kind` ∈ `list | table | board | calendar | form` (the GenUI catalog maps
each kind to one component) and the query whose rows it renders (every kind but a form has
one).

columns.description:
The fields the view shows, in order: a list or table row's cells (the first is the
primary line), a board card's fields (the first is the card title), a calendar event's
details, a form's inputs (a `derived` field renders read-only). Each is an aspect field
or a promoted column (`title`, `type`, `updated_at`); a form shows neither `type` nor
`updated_at`. Empty = the client chooses.

group_by.description:
A board's lanes (GenUI `Board.columns`): the values of this enum field in declared
order, each with the label and tone the field's `display` gives it. On a list or table
it makes sections. A calendar or form has none.

icon.description:
A name in the client's icon set (`[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`); a name the client does not
know renders without an icon.

label.description:
The view's name for people (a tab title, say), as plain text (render it as text, never
as markup).

order.description:
The order a client presents the rows in, within each lane or section when grouped.
Empty = the query's own `order`. It reorders only the rows the query returned and never
changes which rows come back, so a page cut at the query's limit is not the top rows by
this order. Every client compares the same way: missing values last in both directions;
an enum by its declared position; datetimes chronologically, a date without a time of
day counting as 00:00 UTC; integers numerically; `false` before `true`; text by Unicode
code point; rows that compare equal keep the order the query returned them in.

ClientSchema.description:
`GET /client/schema`: the merged meta-schema every client renders forms / boards /
calendars from. `hash` identifies the exact schema (sha256 of its canonical JSON).
ClientSchema.title: ClientSchema

platform_supported.description: Whether this daemon build/platform can serve `keychain-sync` (Apple platforms).

synchronizable.description:
keychain-sync: whether this device's items are synchronizable (`false` =
ThisDeviceOnly). Always `true` in File mode.

ClientSendMessageRequest.description:
The body of `POST /client/messages`. The idempotency key is envelope-level
(`ClientRequest.idempotency_key`), NOT in the body.

payload.description: UTF-8 text payload delivered to the target's mailbox.

to.description: Target agent id (agent-style; must exist in the tree).

ClientSendMessageRequest.title: ClientSendMessageRequest

ClientSetProviderKeyRequest.description:
The body of `POST /client/providers/{provider_id}:set-key`. SENSITIVE: `Debug` is redacted
and the value is never echoed by any response, warning, error or audit record.
ClientSetProviderKeyRequest.title: ClientSetProviderKeyRequest

namespace.description: keychain-sync only: the item namespace. Absent → unchanged.

synchronizable.description:
keychain-sync only: `false` opts this device out of sync (ThisDeviceOnly items;
already-synced items are read through and never deleted). Absent → unchanged.

ClientSkillEntry.description:
An active skill (client-safe projection). Carries provenance + trust metadata but NOT the skill
content or tags.
ClientSkillEntry.title: ClientSkillEntry

ClientMcpEntry.description: An MCP callable tool (client-safe projection; carries the MCP `server_id` provenance).

ClientSkillEntry.description:
An active skill (client-safe projection). Carries provenance + trust metadata but NOT the skill
content or tags.

ClientToolInventory.description: The `GET /client/tools` response payload: grant-filtered WASM + MCP callables + active skills.
ClientToolInventory.title: ClientToolInventory

ClientAgentLlm.description:
The typed `llm:` policy block of an agent's config document (lane agent-llm-policy): the
provider the agent is pinned to, its default model hint, and a hard placement constraint.
Every field is optional. On create/update the block is replaced as a whole; `{}` clears it.

model.description: Default model hint (an alias key or a literal model id); an explicit per-call model wins.

provider.description:
An `llm-providers[].id` of the runtime config (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`). Must name a
configured provider; a request naming another id is `invalid_request` +
details `["unknown_provider"]`. A pinned provider that later disappears from the config
makes the agent's LLM calls fail closed (never a silent fallback).

ClientUpdateAgentRequest.description: The body of `POST /client/agents/{agent_id}:update`. At least one field is required.

capabilities.description:
Full replacement of a CHILD agent's persisted capability list (subset-gated against the
parent; applies at the next daemon start — the live node keeps its current set). The
root agent's capabilities live in its config document, so this field is refused for it.

config_yaml.description: Full replacement of `.agent/config.yaml` (validated by the provider before the write).

handle.description:
A new handle (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, unique). The id and every store keyed by it are
untouched; the live mailbox keeps the old key until the next daemon start.

llm.description:
Whole-block replacement of the agent's `llm:` policy (`{}` clears it). Applies at the
agent's next LLM call — no `restart_required`. Allowed for the root agent too.

ClientUpdateAgentRequest.title: ClientUpdateAgentRequest

ClientProviderAgentCli.description:
An `agent-cli` entry's vendor CLI (ADR 2026-09-28): which vendor, the absolute path of the
user's own unmodified binary, and extra args appended after the fixed no-tools recipe.
Echoed in summaries (a client renders the vendor and offers the vendor's own sign-in
command); it carries no credential.

ClientProviderCost.description: Per-million-token prices (USD) of one provider entry.

ClientProviderRateLimit.description: The provider's rate limit (required by the runtime for every entry).

ClientProviderSidecar.description:
A local-class provider's sidecar launch spec. Request-only: an absolute host command path is
never echoed back (summaries report `sidecar_present`).

ClientWarning.description: A non-fatal, client-safe advisory attached to any envelope (e.g. an idempotent-replay note).
ClientWarning.title: ClientWarning

LlmDeltaWirePage.description:
The WIRE form of a delta page (what the WS pump sends): identical to [`LlmDeltaPage`]
except `cursor` carries the AEAD-SEALED reconnect token (`SealPurpose::DeltaCursor`,
minted at the last included item's boundary — pin ix: cursors mint ONLY at wire-item
boundaries) instead of the plain DTO. `None` when no item shipped or when no cursor
codec is wired (fail closed: page without a resume token, never a plain cursor).
